newsitem.title: USA: CIA chief cites growing power to pierce terrorists.
newsitem.headline: CIA chief cites growing power to pierce terrorists.

text.p: The Central Intelligence Agency has greatly boosted its ability to penetrate terrorist groups and their alleged state sponsors such as Iraq over the past 18 months, CIA Director John Deutch said on Thursday.

Deutch, in a speech on foreign terrorism at Georgetown University, said the spy agency had "substantially increased the number of new sources reporting to us about terrorist groups. The gain of new sources in the past 18 months far exceeds previous achievements."
Deutch, who took over as the top U.S. spymaster 16 months ago, said funds earmarked for piercing terrorist groups had been "sharply" increased. He gave no details.

In reply to questions, he said Iraqi President Saddam Hussein had "spit in the eye" of the world community by breaching truce terms that ended the 1991 Gulf War. He said Saddam would remain a "destabilizing" force in the Middle East so long as he remained in power.

Intelligence information obtained by the CIA and Federal Bureau of Investigation "conclusively" showed that Saddam was behind an alleged Iraqi plot to kill former U.S. President George Bush during a 1993 visit to Kuwait, the CIA chief said.
The United States lists Iraq as one of seven alleged state sponsors of terrorism, along with Cuba, Iran, Libya, North Korea, Sudan and Syria.

Despite the growing U.S. intelligence focus on thwarting foreign guerrillas, "we must anticipate new attempts against American citizens, against our troops and facilities, both here and abroad," Deutch said.

He declined to discuss any guerrilla response that Saddam might be preparing to retaliate for two days' of U.S. missile strikes against southern Iraq. The U.S. strikes were meant to punish Saddam for sending his troops into a Western-protected safe-haven for ethnic Kurds in Iraq's north.
